message.content:
I don’t have a way to probe your connection from here, so I can’t tell you the exact speed right now.  
But you can quickly find out by running a speed‑test yourself. Here are a few easy options:

| Method | How to run it | Notes |
|--------|---------------|-------|
| **Web site** | Open a browser and go to <https://www.speedtest.net> (or <https://fast.com>) | Works on any device with a browser. |
| **Command line (Linux/macOS)** | `speedtest-cli` (install via `pip install speedtest-cli` if you don’t have it) | Run `speedtest-cli` in a terminal. |
| **Command line (Windows)** | If you have PowerShell, you can use the free `speedtest-cli` as well: `pip install speedtest-cli` then `speedtest-cli`. | Requires Python and pip. |
| **Built‑in Windows tool** | `Test-NetConnection -ComputerName www.google.com -Port 443` | Gives latency and packet loss, not throughput. |

If you’re on a Windows machine and want a quick command‑line test, you can try this (assuming Python is installed):

```powershell
pip install speedtest-cli
speedtest-cli
```

That will output your download and upload speeds in Mbps.

Let me know if you need help installing or running any of these tools!
